meeting_header: Date: 2026-08-14 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Riley Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Tom Rivers (CTO - Helio), Carlos Mendez (Head of ML - Helio), Aisha Khan (Platform Eng - Helio)
summary: Helio Labs is evaluating options to move serving from their vLLM/TGI stack and OpenAI calls to a unified provider. Major concerns: perf parity with current vLLM setup, cost per token, and security (VPC + KMS). Redwood AE/SE positioned hosted -> dedicated -> private options and agreed to run a tailored benchmark and deliver security docs.
topics: Current stack and pain: vLLM + TGI + OpenAI fallback
Eval parity: prompts, metrics (latency, p95, token cost, quality)
Hosting tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) and network egress/residency
Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00:03] Riley: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Riley from Redwood, AE on this account. Um, quick intro before we dive — Priya's our SE and will take most of the technical questions.
[00:00:12] Tom: Hi, Tom Rivers here. I'll jump in where strategy and ops intersect.
[00:00:18] Carlos: Carlos Mendez, Head of ML. We're running vLLM + TGI in-house for inference and still using OpenAI for some tasks.
[00:00:25] Aisha: Aisha, platform team, I'll be looking at networking and deployment constraints.
[00:00:33] Riley: Awesome. Quick agenda — we want to understand your current footprint, main pain points, what parity looks like, and then cover hosting options and security. Does that work?
[00:00:40] Tom: Yes, go ahead.
[00:00:44] Carlos: We have a pile of prompts and a few critical gen endpoints. Latency at p95 matters for user-facing features; cost is also huge. Right now vLLM gives us good latency locally, but maintenance and ops are heavy.
[00:00:55] Priya: Understood. Can you give ballpark numbers for throughput, average seq length, and token volumes?
[00:01:01] Carlos: Sure — avg sequence 220 tokens, p95 around 400, about 1.2M tokens/day across all endpoints, spikes to 3–4x during peak.
[00:01:10] Aisha: We also have strict data residency for EU users and want KMS for customer data encryption at rest.
[00:01:16] Riley: Good context. Two immediate things: parity is both perf and quality. We can run a side-by-side eval with your prompts — Redwood hosted first, then dedicated or private if you need VPC.
[00:01:28] Carlos: What's the delta we should expect compared to our vLLM setup? We tuned kernels and use kv cache tricks.
[00:01:34] Priya: So vLLM/TGI often benefits from close-to-metal optimizations and your own kernel choices. Our runtime includes attention optimizations, automatic KV caching, and quantization paths — for many models the latency is within 5–15% of tuned vLLM for similar hardware and usually lower ops cost due to batching and smart routing. But we'll validate with your exact workload.
[00:01:50] Tom: And cost? We need concrete numbers — tokens cost, GPU ops, reserved pool pricing.
[00:01:56] Riley: We'll share pricing models: hosted per-token, dedicated reserved capacity, and private license+support. For pilots we typically suggest hosted to get baseline metrics then move to dedicated if you need predictable throughput.
[00:02:06] Aisha: Important: our security team requires SOC2, SSO via SAML, RBAC, and audit logs for all calls. Can Redwood support bringing-your-own-KMS and VPC peering?
[00:02:15] Priya: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC options. RBAC and audit logs are available in the Console. We'll include the SOC2 report and KMS integration notes in the security pack.
[00:02:24] Riley: I'll send the security pack after the call.
[00:02:27] Carlos: On model compatibility — we run a mix of open models and some fine-tuned versions. Can you host customer fine-tunes, or do we need to port them?
[00:02:33] Priya: You can bring model weights for Private/Dedicated. For Hosted we can support hosted variants and work with you on onboarding fine-tunes; there are compatibility checks for tokenizer and model config. We also surface model variants in our catalog.
[00:02:45] Tom: Any gotchas with tokenizer mismatch? Our tokenization sometimes changes outputs.
[00:02:49] Priya: Tokenizer mismatch is a common source of divergence. Our onboarding includes a tokenizer parity check and sample generation comparison. We'll flag mismatch and either convert or recommend minor retrains.
[00:02:59] Riley: We also run quality evals with your prompt set and hold regression alerts if we see drift.
[00:03:05] Carlos: Good. We use TGI for some batching and GPU sharing semantics — do you interop with TGI or is that a re-architect?
[00:03:12] Priya: TGI is compatible as an orchestration approach; if you export the model artifacts we can run them in our runtime. There are sometimes ops-level differences (worker recycling, batching windows). We'll capture that in the benchmark.
[00:03:23] Aisha: Latency SLA — can you hit p95 < 250ms for our small completion endpoints?
[00:03:29] Priya: Depends on model family and sequence length. For smaller models and trimmed seq lengths we often hit sub-200ms p95 on dedicated GPUs. For larger models p95 will be higher. We'll include p50/p95/p99 in the perf run.
[00:03:40] Tom: What about fallback? If hosted has an outage, can we automatically failover to dedicated or to a cheaper variant?
[00:03:46] Riley: Yes — Redwood supports smart routing policies and automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants or regions. You can set routing by latency, cost, or capacity.
[00:03:56] Carlos: For the eval, we need you to mirror our request patterns including bursts. Can you simulate token distribution?
[00:04:02] Priya: Absolutely. If you share the prompt corpus and trace-level token histogram, we can replay realistic traffic including bursts and measure tails.
[00:04:09] Aisha: On networking, we prefer VPC peering for Private. Any egress charges we'd need to plan for?
[00:04:15] Riley: Egress depends on deployment. Private on-prem obviously keeps traffic internal; cloud Private or Dedicated in customer VPC reduces egress for intra-VPC calls but external users will have standard cloud egress. We'll map costs in the pilot.
[00:04:27] Tom: Legal — Do you have standard DPA and data residency clauses?
[00:04:31] Riley: Yes, we have a DPA and templates. I'll attach them.
[00:04:35] Carlos: Can you run a short head-to-head today-ish? We can't wait weeks.
[00:04:39] Priya: We can start a quick smoke benchmark in 48–72 hours for hosted: ingest your prompt set, run 1k samples per model. For the full evaluation (burst + tails + dedicated profiling) we'll need about 10 working days.
[00:04:52] Aisha: Who does the onboarding for Private? If we go private, what’s the timeline?
[00:04:56] Priya: Private deployments vary; standard on-prem or VPC packages are typically 6–8 weeks for integration, less if you take our managed options. Dedicated reserved pools can be provisioned in 2–3 weeks.
[00:05:06] Tom: Ok. I want explicit rollback plans — if we move a feature to Redwood and see quality regression, how fast can we switch back to OpenAI or our vLLM?
[00:05:13] Riley: We recommend canary rollouts and automatic fallbacks. You can pin AB tests to model versions; if quality drops beyond thresholds we fail back to the previous provider.
[00:05:21] Carlos: About cost: we saw in your docs some quantization and batching suggestions. How much can quantization degrade quality?
[00:05:27] Priya: Quantization depends on model and task. 8-bit often preserves quality for many tasks, but we'll run evals that measure generation quality (BLEU, ROUGE, human scoring when needed) vs the baseline and report.
[00:05:38] Riley: We'll also surface recommendation which configs maximize cost savings while keeping quality within your thresholds.
[00:05:43] Tom: Competitors asked: why pick Redwood vs sticking with OpenAI or Anthropic?
[00:05:47] Riley: Main reasons clients pick Redwood: predictable economics across deployments, unified tooling for ops and traceability, and the ability to run in customer-controlled environments (Private) which is critical for regulated workloads. Also our routing and caching reduces per-token ops.
[00:05:59] Aisha: We have one specific security Q — HSM-backed customer KMS for model keys and audit trail retention for 2 years.
[00:06:06] Priya: Our Private deployment supports HSM/KMS integrations and audit log retention windows can be extended via add-on. We'll include the retention SLA in the pack.
[00:06:14] Carlos: Cool. Any friction with model formats? We have some fine-tunes in safetensors and a couple in Transformers checkpoint format.
[00:06:20] Priya: We support common formats; safetensors typically works fine. If there are edge cases we'll convert and test. We'll flag any incompatible custom ops.
[00:06:29] Riley: Let's outline the pilot: 1) share prompt corpus and token histogram; 2) Redwood runs hosted perf baseline with your prompts; 3) compare to your vLLM baseline; 4) propose dedicated sizing if you need sustained throughput.
[00:06:43] Tom: Sounds good. Timeline real quick?
[00:06:46] Priya: If you share artifacts tomorrow, hosted smoke in 48–72h, perf spreadsheet by next Friday, then deeper dedicated sizing week after.
[00:06:56] Aisha: One more ops question: tracing — can we correlate user requests to logs for debugging?
[00:07:01] Riley: Yes, we expose request IDs and per-route tracing in the console; you can hook into tracing hooks for APM correlation.
[00:07:08] Carlos: Ok let's talk about cost modeling quickly — are there reserved pool discounts for predictable commits?
[00:07:12] Riley: Yes, Dedicated reserved capacity has tiered discounts and we can show example math for your token volumes.
[00:07:18] Tom: On legal, we'll need a contact for SOC2 and DPA questions.
[00:07:21] Riley: I'll be the initial contact and will introduce you to our security team in the email.
[00:07:27] Aisha: For the perf run, what metrics will you provide?
[00:07:31] Priya: We'll provide p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens, failure/error rates, and a quality delta vs your baseline.
[00:07:41] Carlos: Include model determinism/seed behavior — that bites us in A/B tests.
[00:07:44] Priya: We'll note deterministic settings and how they affect outputs; we can run seeded evals.
[00:07:50] Riley: Anything else we should cover?
[00:07:52] Tom: I'd like an example of a rollback playbook on paper.
[00:07:55] Priya: We'll include a 1-page rollback and canary runbook as part of the pilot deliverables.
[00:08:01] Carlos: Great. Also please note we have a small internal eval that uses multi-turn chat and RAG — might need embedding parity too.
[00:08:08] Priya: Embeddings: we have multiple embedding backends and can reproduce your vectors and compare cosine distance/regression on retrieval. We'll include that.
[00:08:16] Aisha: Ok, next steps recap?
[00:08:19] Riley: I'll send the security pack and DPA, attach a pilot template, and include pricing options. Priya will run the hosted smoke and perf runs once you share prompts.
[00:08:28] Carlos: We'll share prompts and token hist by tomorrow EOD.
[00:08:32] Tom: Let's tentatively schedule the deep dive week of the 24th.
[00:08:36] Riley: Noted. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links (security pack, deck, benchmark spreadsheet).
[00:08:42] Aisha: Thanks, bye.
[00:08:45] Tom: Thanks.
[00:08:47] Carlos: Bye.
[00:08:50] Riley: (post-call note) sending links: security-pack.pdf, pilot-template.xlsx, perf-spreadsheet.csv — (link placeholders).
